title: Close moves an earlier bill from Cost of Parts to the category's account
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Complete, with one special-order part whose vendor bill of $125.00 posted to Cost of Parts while billable, then moved to customer B, so it is internal.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • A reclass entry debits account X $125.00 and credits Cost of Parts $125.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R4: “When a vendor bill was posted to Cost of Parts (or a category account) and the work order later becomes internal or no charge, Close adds a reclass journal entry: debit the mapped expense account, credit the account the bill line was posted to, for that bill's lines. When a vendor bill was posted to one expense account and the work order closes under the other classification, Close adds a reclass from the account the bill line was posted to, to the work order's mapped account; no reclass when both resolve to the same account. When a vendor bill was posted to an expense account and the work order becomes billable, invoicing adds the reverse entry: debit the account the bill would post to today, credit that expense account.”
  • S2-R8: “If a vendor bill already exists on the work order, a customer change (S2-R7), a Convert action (S2-R5, S2-R6) or, on a line that has a posted vendor bill, Mark as No Charge, Change category or Mark as Billable (Story 12) first shows the dialog "Change where the cost is posted?" with the body "The vendor bill for [part] ($[amount]) was posted to [account]. If you continue, that cost moves to [account] when this work order is [invoiced / closed]." For several bills: "The vendor bills for [n] parts ($[total]) were posted to [account]. ..." Buttons: Cancel and "Continue". The account names are the shop's own mapping rows (Cost of Parts, or the expense account of a category); between the expense accounts of two categories the dialog names both. Not shown when the location has no accounting integration.”
